newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African investors looking for gold opportunities.
newsitem.headline: S.African investors looking for gold opportunities.

text.p: Most South African asset managers had cut their gold holdings to minimal levels before the recent price slide and some said on Wednesday they were already looking for buying opportunities.
"We've taken a fair bit of pain but now we'd rather be looking for buying opportunities than to get rid of the little bit we still hold," said Old Mutual portfolio manager Jeremy Bolton.
Total assets in the group's mining and gold funds had fallen from 1.2 billion rand ($265 million) on March 31 to below one billion at the end of June, he said.
Bolton said Old Mutual, the country's biggest asset manager, had not taken a position on the likely bottom of the slide but would be looking for signs of a temporary end to the fall.
Gold traded around 12-year lows on Wednesday after falling sharply last Friday. The Johannesburg Stock Exchange all-gold index was orbiting the 900 level, down from 1,500 at the end of February.
One Cape Town-based gold analyst who asked not to be named said it would be virtually impossible to predict the price at which gold would bottom out.
But he said it would rebound to above $360 an ounce.
"We were short golds and we took a position at $340. Since then it's been pretty sore but I'm going to tough it out.
"When the bounce comes, I don't think any fund manager will be able to afford to be out of golds altogether," he said.
Infinity Asset management analyst Grahame Graham-Parker was less optimistic, saying gold could languish once the bottom is reached.
"I think there will be a nice bounce in the underlying commodity but the companies are going to have to rebuild before there is a dividend for investors," he said.
Ivan Palframan, general manager portfolio management for the Syfrets investment company, said his fund managers had shed golds in advance of the recent slide.
Even the group's 60 million rand Mining Resources Unit Trust was light on gold shares and overweight on mining financials.
"We're not seeing any strong selling by our investors at present but it could still come," he said.

Board of Executors general manager John Winship said his group had reduced the gold-share allocation among its funds to between one and two percent of assets under management well ahead of the latest slump.
He said the group would watch for buying opportunities as the slide slowed but he did not expect to significantly increase the gold-share allocation above its current level.
